pc.ai.cleared: Conversation cleared. The model keeps no other memory.
pc.ai.emptyOutput: The model gave an empty answer. Try rephrasing.
pc.ai.generatedIn: Generated in %@ s on this computer
pc.ai.model.none: OSHI does not ship model weights with the desktop app. Choose a .gguf file you already have.
pc.ai.model.notGguf: %@ is not a GGUF model file.
pc.ai.model.title: Model
pc.ai.modelGone: The chosen model can no longer be used: %@
pc.ai.nativeMissing: The local AI engine (llama.cpp) is not available on this computer: %@
pc.ai.noModel: No model is chosen yet. Choose a .gguf file first.
pc.ai.noNative: The llama.cpp engine is not installed on this computer.
pc.ai.setup.body: Answers are generated on this computer and nothing is uploaded. It needs a .gguf model file and the llama.cpp engine.
pc.ai.timedOut: No answer after %d s. Nothing partial is shown.
pc.call.audio.none: Connected — no audio devices on this machine
pc.call.devices.cameraDefaultOnly: This Mac uses its default camera.
pc.call.devices.nextCall: Microphone and speaker changes apply from your next call.
pc.call.micBlocked.mac: The other person can't hear you: your microphone is sending pure silence. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone and allow OSHI.
pc.call.micBlocked.other: The other person can't hear you: your microphone is sending pure silence. Check that the microphone is not muted in your system sound settings.
pc.call.micBlocked.windows: The other person can't hear you: your microphone is sending pure silence. Open Windows Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone and turn on "Let desktop apps access your microphone".
pc.covert.carrier.hint: Copy all of it. It reads like the cover text and carries the message in invisible characters; anything that rewrites the text destroys it.
pc.covert.cover.room: This cover can carry about %d characters of message. Longer cover, more room.
pc.covert.for.hint: Only this contact can open it, and not even you later unless you keep the original.
pc.covert.limits.desktop: For now it works between computers only. The phones understand the format but have no screen for it yet.
pc.covert.limits.forward: It has no forward secrecy: the key comes from your two identities and never changes. Ordinary OSHI messages do not work this way.
pc.covert.limits.title: What covert text does not do
pc.covert.limits.visible: It hides a message from a reader, not from an analyst: the hidden characters can be found by anyone who inspects the bytes, and a site that strips them destroys the message.
pc.covert.message.placeholder: What you really want to say
pc.covert.noContacts: A covert message is for one person: it only opens with the key you share with them. Add a contact first.
pc.covert.paste.hint: Paste it exactly as it arrived. Retyping or reformatting removes the hidden characters.
pc.covert.refused: This cover text cannot carry a message. Try another one.
pc.covert.subtitle: Hide a message inside ordinary text. OSHI does not send it: you copy it and carry it any way you like.
pc.covert.title: Covert text
pc.covert.tooShort: The cover text is too short: it holds %1$d bytes and this message needs %2$d. Lengthen the cover or shorten the message.
pc.covert.unknownPeer: This contact's address cannot be used.
pc.covert.unreadable: Nothing readable for this contact: it carries nothing, it is for someone else, or it was changed on the way.
pc.devices.forceOn: Turn it on on this computer
pc.devices.forceOn.hint: Off: follow the server, which decides when direct sync opens to everyone.
pc.devices.mailbox.badApproval: That approval was not accepted. Link this computer again from your other device.
pc.devices.mailbox.conflict: This computer's device key is already used by another device. Its mailbox cannot be set up.
pc.devices.mailbox.error: Could not reach the server to set up this computer's mailbox. It will try again.
pc.devices.mailbox.holder: Messages from contacts on older versions of OSHI also arrive on this computer.
pc.devices.mailbox.needsApproval: Approve this computer from one of your other devices: link it above and allow it there.
pc.devices.mailbox.newDevice: A new device was added to your account. If it was not you, remove it below.
pc.devices.mailbox.notHolder: Messages from contacts on older versions of OSHI arrive on your other device and reach this computer at the next sync.
pc.devices.mailbox.off: Per-device delivery is not switched on by the server yet. This computer shares your account's mailbox, as before.
pc.devices.mailbox.registered: This computer has its own mailbox: messages from up-to-date contacts reach it even while your phone is off.
pc.devices.mailbox.removed.body: It no longer receives its own copy of your messages. To receive them again, link it from another of your devices.
pc.devices.mailbox.removed.title: This computer was removed from your OSHI account
pc.devices.mailbox.title: Delivery to this computer
pc.devices.mailbox.tooMany: Your account already has the maximum of 8 devices. Remove one to add this computer.
pc.devices.mailbox.unregistered: This computer does not have its own mailbox yet.
pc.devices.on: Your history moves device to device, over the local network or through a relay that stores nothing.
pc.devices.peerApproved: The other device already approved. Approve here to finish.
pc.devices.wants: %1$@ (%2$@) wants to receive your history. Check that its screen shows the same code.
pc.limits.bluetooth.title: Pairing a radio over Bluetooth
pc.limits.bluetooth.why: The desktop runtime has no Bluetooth. Connect the radio with a USB cable (macOS, Linux) or over the network (all systems).
pc.limits.camera.title: Scanning a QR code with the camera
pc.limits.camera.why: Not every computer has a camera. Open a picture or screenshot of the code instead, or paste its text.
pc.limits.gps.title: Your location and check-ins
pc.limits.gps.why: A computer has no GPS, and OSHI does not guess your position from Wi-Fi or your IP address. Locations you receive still show; a radio can announce a position you type in.
pc.limits.ledger.hint: The engineering ledger behind this list, in English, row by row.
pc.limits.nearby.title: Finding people nearby without a network
pc.limits.nearby.why: Phones find each other over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct. A computer finds OSHI devices on the same network, or reaches them through a LoRa radio.
pc.limits.push.title: Notifications while OSHI is closed
pc.limits.push.why: Phones are woken by Apple and Google push services; computers have no equivalent for OSHI. Messages arrive while OSHI runs, also from the menu bar or tray, and are waiting when you open it.
pc.limits.screenshot.title: Blocking screenshots
pc.limits.screenshot.why: No system offers it reliably: Linux has no way at all, and on recent macOS screen recorders can still capture a protected window. A switch that promised it would be a false promise.
pc.limits.subtitle: Things a computer cannot do, and why
pc.limits.systemAi.title: Apple Intelligence
pc.limits.systemAi.why: It is only available inside Apple's phone and tablet apps. The desktop uses a model that runs on your computer instead.
pc.limits.title: What the computer app cannot do
pc.limits.watch.title: Apple Watch and Wear OS
pc.limits.watch.why: A watch pairs with a phone, not with a computer.
pc.mail.alias.confirmRemove: Remove the alias %@? Mail sent to it will no longer arrive.
pc.mail.draftTextOnly: Drafts keep text only. Send the message, or remove the attachments before saving it as a draft.
pc.mail.drive.confirmDelete: Delete this file for ever? There is no copy to recover it from.
pc.mail.err.attachDrive: Could not attach the drive file.
pc.mail.err.attachmentsTotal: Attachments together may not exceed 18 MB.
pc.mail.err.downloadDrive: Could not download the drive file.
pc.mail.err.draftChanged: The draft changed before the drive file finished downloading.
pc.mail.err.draftNotRemoved: Message sent, but its draft could not be removed: %@
pc.mail.err.failed: That did not work. Try again.
pc.mail.err.qrNotPairing: That QR code is not a mail pairing request.
pc.mail.err.qrUnreadable: Could not read a QR code in this image.
pc.mail.err.quotaUsed: You have used all of this month's 150 messages.
pc.mail.err.sessions: Could not load the connected browsers.
pc.mail.err.signout: Could not sign that browser out.
pc.mail.newBrowser: A new browser can read this mailbox: %@. If it was not you, sign it out.
pc.mail.reader.emptyBody: Choose a message on the left to read it here.
pc.map.err.region: A region file could not be read: %@
pc.map.limits.gps: Find where you are. A computer has no GPS and OSHI does not guess your position from Wi-Fi or your IP address.
pc.map.limits.regions: Download regions. Search reads the region files already on this computer, the same files the phones download.
pc.map.limits.route: Navigate turn by turn. There is no routing engine on the desktop yet.
pc.map.limits.tiles: The map pictures come from oshi-messenger.com, which therefore sees the area you look at. While OSHI traffic is disguised, none are downloaded.
pc.map.limits.title: What the map cannot do on a computer
pc.map.noRegions.body: The map works without them. To search places and streets offline, copy the region files from a phone into this folder:
pc.map.noRegions.title: No offline regions on this computer
pc.map.tilesOffline: Map pictures are not downloaded while OSHI traffic is disguised
pc.peers.announce: Announce this computer and look for others
pc.peers.announce.hint: Both at once: turning this off also stops announcing your name and key on the network. Open connections are left alone.
pc.peers.badAddress: Give an address and a port from 1 to 65535.
pc.peers.byHand.hint: When discovery cannot see a device (another subnet, or mDNS blocked). Its identity is still checked when it connects.
pc.peers.disconnected: Disconnected from %@. Discovery may reconnect; to stop that, block them or turn scanning off.
pc.peers.empty.body: A device appears here within seconds of joining the same network. If one never does, the two are probably on different subnets, or mDNS is blocked.
pc.peers.empty.title: Nobody found yet
pc.peers.meshOff.body: This window was started without --mesh, so nothing is announced or looked for. Start OSHI with --mesh to find devices on this network.
pc.peers.meshOff.title: The local network mesh is off
pc.peers.notice.meshOff: The local network mesh is not running in this window, so there is nothing to announce. Start OSHI with --mesh; until then this list stays empty.
pc.peers.notice.off: Scanning off. Nothing is announced and nothing is looked for; open connections are left alone.
pc.peers.notice.on: Scanning. This computer is visible on the network again.
pc.peers.notice.refused: Discovery did not start. The mesh is running, so the network is refusing multicast; it is not a setting.
pc.peers.subtitle: OSHI devices on this network, with no internet needed
pc.peers.title: Nearby peers
pc.radio.adopt.none: Nothing to change: this node already has a name somebody chose.
pc.radio.airtime.detail: Share of the last hour spent transmitting
pc.radio.beacon.told: The radio has been told. It announces a fixed position about every 6 hours, so other radios may take that long to show it.
pc.radio.broadcast.hint: Plain Meshtastic text on the public channel: every Meshtastic radio in range can read it. Not encrypted by OSHI.
pc.radio.broadcast.sent: Handed to the radio. Anyone in range can read it.
pc.radio.broadcast.title: Say something on the mesh
pc.radio.connect.title: Connect a radio
pc.radio.hostRefused: That address was refused: no spaces, and a port from 1 to 65535.
pc.radio.link: This radio belongs to a contact…
pc.radio.link.ambiguous: Refused: this radio's own evidence contradicted itself, so it is linked to nobody.
pc.radio.link.bound: Linked to %@. Its plain Meshtastic text now appears in that conversation, unauthenticated.
pc.radio.link.conflict: Refused: this radio already proved it belongs to someone else with a message that decrypted.
pc.radio.link.rejected: Refused: that contact has no usable OSHI key.
pc.radio.map.caption: Distance and bearing from this radio. Circles show estimated reach; relayed nodes get none.
pc.radio.map.noFix: The range diagram needs this radio's own position, and it has no GPS fix yet.
pc.radio.map.noNodes: No node has reported a position yet.
pc.radio.media.hint: Off by default. Over the radio an attachment can be about %d bytes at most: an icon or a contact card, not a photo.
pc.radio.notAttached.body: Plug a Meshtastic radio in over USB or connect to one on your network. OSHI then sends over LoRa when there is no internet.
pc.radio.notSent: Not sent. The radio log says why.
pc.radio.oshi.hint: End-to-end encrypted, over the radio, with no internet. Radios in range carry it; only this contact can read it.
pc.radio.oshi.sent: Encrypted and handed to the radio. Radio messages are not acknowledged, so it will say sent, not delivered.
pc.radio.oshi.title: Message a contact off the grid
pc.radio.position.first: Save a position first: there is nothing to beacon yet.
pc.radio.position.footer: Off by default. The radio then announces this position UNENCRYPTED to every radio in range, up to tens of kilometres away, including strangers. The position stays stored on the radio until you forget it.
pc.radio.position.forgotten: Position forgotten, and the beacon is off.
pc.radio.position.hint: A computer has no GPS. Type where this radio is; nothing guesses it from Wi-Fi or your address.
pc.radio.position.invalid: Not a position on Earth: latitude −90 to 90, longitude −180 to 180, and 0, 0 is not a place.
pc.radio.position.saved: Position saved. Nothing is broadcast until you turn the beacon on.
pc.radio.preferRadio.hint: The radio is tried first. If nothing comes back within %d seconds, the internet takes the message.
pc.radio.refused: The radio did not accept it. The radio log says why.
pc.radio.region.asked: Asked the radio for %@. The card updates when the node reports back.
pc.radio.region.footer: Which frequencies and power a radio may use is set by law and differs by country. Choose where the radio is actually used.
pc.radio.traffic.hint: The last frames in and out of the radio: kind, size and node. Never their content.
pc.radio.unlinked: Unlinked. Its text goes back to its own radio conversation.
pc.radio.usb.none: No USB radio found. Plug the radio in.
pc.radio.usb.unsupported: On this computer a radio connects over the network only.
pc.sched.empty.body: Choose who, type the message, then choose when it should go out.
pc.sched.empty.title: Nothing scheduled
pc.sched.exactHint: Or type an exact date and time: year-month-day hour:minute.
pc.sched.howItWorks: A scheduled message goes out on the first check after its time. If OSHI is closed then, it goes out late, the next time OSHI opens, and says so. Nothing wakes this computer.
pc.sched.noRecipients: Add a contact or join a group before scheduling a message.
pc.sched.subtitle: Saved on this computer only
